newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF to cut 6-yr JGB volume in auction--traders.
newsitem.headline: MOF to cut 6-yr JGB volume in auction--traders.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is likely to reduce the volume of six-year Japanese government bonds (JGB) in its price-competitive auction expected on Tuesday, traders said on Monday.
The MOF officials were not immediately available for comment.
The MOF showed its intention to reduce the offering volume of six-year JGBs when it consulted market participants on Monday morning about demand for the new bonds, traders said.
When the MOF last auctioned six-year bonds on May 8, it offered 500 billion yen worth at a coupon rate of 1.8 percent.

Traders said if the MOF continues to conduct a six-year JGN auction every other month, the ministry could raise far more than it has planned for this fiscal year. The MOF is now expected to offer 400 billion yen of six-year JGBs, instead of 500 billion yen expected earlier, in Tuesday's auction and in subsequent auctions, they said. The MOF has said it plans to raise 2.4 trillion yen by issuing six-year JGBs in the year started on April 1, 1997, unchanged from a year earlier. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
